See also: Agitation

English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
agitation
Wikipedia

Etymology

[edit]

From French agitation, from Latin agitātiō (“movement, agitation”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ædʒ.ɪˈteɪ.ʃən/
    • Audio (US):(file)
  • (Indic) IPA(key): /ə.dʒɪˈʈe.ʃən/
  • Rhymes: -eɪʃən

Noun

[edit]

agitation (countable and uncountable, plural agitations)

  1. The act of agitating, or the state of being agitated; the state of being disrupted with violence, or with irregular action; commotion.
    During a storm the sea is in agitation.
  2. A disturbance of personal tranquillity; disturbance of someone's peace of mind.
    Synonym: perturbation
    She causes great agitation within me.
  3. Excitement of public feeling by discussion, appeals, etc.
    the antislavery agitation
    labor agitation
    After this conflict pro-independence agitation temporarily died down.
    • 1855–1858, William H[ickling] Prescott, History of the Reign of Philip the Second, King of Spain, volume (please specify |volume=I to III), Boston, Mass.: Phillips, Sampson, and Company, →OCLC:
      […] religious agitations […]
  4. (archaic) Examination or consideration of a subject in controversy, or of a plan proposed for adoption; earnest discussion; debate.
    • 1692, Roger L’Estrange, “ (please specify the fable number.) (please specify the name of the fable.)”, in Fables, of Æsop and Other Eminent Mythologists: […], London: […] R[ichard] Sare, […], →OCLC:
      […] a logical agitation of the matter […]
    • 1732, Jonathan Swift, The Advantages Proposed by Repealing the Sacramental Test:
      […] the project now in agitation […]
  5. Putting into motion by shaking or stirring, often to achieve mixing.

Synonyms

[edit]
  • emotion, commotion, excitement, trepidation, tremor, perturbation

Derived terms

[edit]
  • agitational
  • agitationist
  • agitprop
  • counteragitation
  • microagitation

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin agitātiōnem. By surface analysis, agiter +‎ -ation.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /a.ʒi.ta.sjɔ̃/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)

Noun

[edit]

agitation f (plural agitations)

  1. choppiness (of water), turbulence (in air), swaying (of branch etc.)
  2. restlessness
  3. bustle (of street, room etc.); activity
  4. (nervous) agitation
  5. (social) unrest

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Dutch: agitatie
    • Afrikaans: agitasie
    • → Indonesian: agitasi
  • → Romanian: agitație
  • → Turkish: ajitasyon

Further reading

[edit]
  • “agitation”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012
